package: case 1351-01 SMT - 8-lead gull-wing SOP at 2.54mm pitch, both ports on one face
notes: *** SOLDERED DIRECTLY TO THE MAIN BOARD - NO SOCKET. *** Case 1351-01 is Surface Mount [ds p.1 ordering table; outline p.7/p.20]. LAND PATTERN: 8 pads 2.80 x 1.52mm at 2.54mm pitch, rows 16.00mm apart centre to centre (outer pad edges 18.80mm apart) - derived on breath-sense-link.md from the 1351 outline, pads lengthened inward for a ~0.5mm heel; the datasheet's Figure 6 is drawn for case 482 [p.6], do not copy its 16.76mm. PINOUT Style 2: pin 2 VS, 3 GND, 4 VOUT, 1 and 5-8 N/C [p.4 Figure 1: 'Pins 1, 5, 6, 7, and 8 are NO CONNECTS for small outline package device'; Style 2 on p.8, p.20] - buzz it out on arrival as a check. Marked face up (P1), ports towards the tail. The spare goes in with an iron, lid off - procedure on breath-sense-link.md. AFTER ANY SWAP: re-mask both ports, power-cycle for the firmware zero and re-null TRIM-BREATH-ZERO (Note 5 p.3). The sheet gives NO soldering conditions: decided by banking NXP's soldering note for its pressure packages. ~1ms response = ~159Hz corner; the loop runs 4kHz and rate lives on the DAC side. DP NOT GP: identical transfer function (see breath-sensor-slope and sensor-full-scale) but in production to 2028 where the GP is obsolete. Full scale is sensor-full-scale, NOT the cover page's span. *** THE REFERENCE PORT IS THE OTHER FACE OF THE SAME DIAPHRAGM, NOT AN OUTLET. *** Left open to the cavity, and it must NEVER be blocked - mask before coating. *** P1 IS 'Side with Part Marking' [Table 3] AND THIS DIFFERS FROM THE GP, *** which is 'Side with Port Attached' on case 1369-01: same family, same transfer function, opposite convention, so a port assignment copied from a GP reference design is wrong. FIGURE 3 IS FITTED (owner, 2026-10-01): 1.0uF and 0.01uF on VS, 470pF on Vout, all three at the sensor on the main board (C-SENSOR-VS-BULK, C-SENSOR-VS-HF, C-SENSOR-OUT). The datasheet's accuracy curves were taken with exactly that circuit [ds p.5], so it is the conservative choice; AN1646's 750 ohm + 0.33uF is NOT fitted, because it would change the conditions the +/-2.46%VFSS was measured under. AN1646 also gives averaging figures: 10 samples ~2.5mV pk-pk, 64 samples ~1mV, or 4 samples behind the RC ~1mV. *** THE AUTOZERO MUST BE RE-TAKEN AS THE SEALED BODY WARMS *** - Note 5, verbatim: 'the device output must be autozeroed after installation... The specified accuracy assumes a maximum temperature change of +-5 degC between autozero and measurement.' TcOffset IS UNSOURCED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS - the datasheet only defines it, never values it - so neither the design's 0.5mV/K nor a derived 2.34mV/K is a datasheet number, and the 2.34 derivation double-counts by assuming the full 50K window where the accuracy figure assumes +/-5C. NEEDS A BENCH MEASUREMENT. Operating range is only +10C to +60C, so a cold room plus a 20K warm-up can take it outside that range. BUY FROM A DISTRIBUTOR: LCSC held 3 on 2026-09-29 [web] against 2 per instrument. Footprint woody:NXP_Case1351-01_SOP-8_P2.54mm (hardware/lib/README.md). Hand-soldered with an iron; the datasheet publishes no soldering profile

description: Series protection on the breath buffer output into the umbilical
notes: TWO, not one, and 1206 not 0805 - both changed with the schematic and this row did not follow. R1 in the BREATH leg, R1b its twin in the AGND leg: the return leg carries no signal current, so a matching resistor costs no differential gain and is what keeps the 1M bias pair from capping CMRR at 60dB on its own. 1206 because ADR 0003's designed-safe sustained +12V fault puts 11.8mA through R1: 139mW against an 0805's ~125mW. Both are instrument-side and UNRETROFITTABLE

description: ESD protection on the BREATH and AGND legs
notes: *** 12V STANDOFF, NOT 5V. *** BREATH's normal top of range is sensor-full-scale, which leaves only 140mV of margin against a 5V array's V_RWM, on the project's DC-accurate output. Worse, ADR 0003's buffer-on-+12V decision exists precisely so a SUSTAINED +12V fault on BREATH is harmless - a 5V clamp turns that designed-safe case into a part that conducts until something fails. PESD12VS1UA,115 (LCSC C131084), SOD-323: VRWM 12 V, VBR 13.3 V min [ds NEXPERIA-PESD12VS1UA.pdf p.5], so a sustained +12 V does not conduct; leakage 100 nA max at 12 V, 0.1 mV across the 1k [calc]. NOT THE UB: PESD12VS1UB is SOD523 [ds NEXPERIA-PESD12VS1UB.pdf p.1], 0402-class. The UA's 180 pF max behind the 1k is a pole at 0.88 MHz, far above the breath band [calc]
